standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws.

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Li--Wager known-rank \(C^3\) class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

definitions.name: Explicit first-projection PC handle with conservative ANOVA certificate
definitions.construction:
Conditionally on \(A\), put \(X=Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n\), \(P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)\), and \(C_A=P_AA\).  For every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), define
\[
 \widetilde\gamma_{i,h}=q_{i,h}-4(C_AX)_i.
\]
Thus only the bandwidth-free first Hoeffding projection is spectrally balanced.  Define the graph-observable certificates
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 =\frac{2B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}|(C_A)_{ii}|
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
       \sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
\]
and
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 =\frac{B^2}{n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}.
\]
The latter is the conservative conditional-Hoeffding certificate obtained by retaining the exact third-and-higher score remainder and applying a final Euclidean Cauchy--Schwarz bound; it is not asserted to have order \(d/n\).

definitions.name: Feasible explicit first-projection PC estimator
definitions.construction:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii for the explicit PC handle
Same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus
definitions.construction: Let \(\pi_{m,n}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}P(N_i\le m)\). Set \(a_0=B\), \(a_m=\min\{Bm^{-1},Lm^{-2}\}\) for \(m\ge1\), and \(\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}=\max_{0\le m\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor}a_m\sqrt{\pi_{m,n}/n}\).

definitions.name: Supported and degree-exact full-class envelopes
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}=\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\}\) and \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)]\).

definitions.name: Absolute-risk and honest-length criteria
definitions.construction: \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P(\theta_n\in\mathcal C)\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]\), where the infima range over measurable procedures based on \((A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=N\geq1\), fix \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), and condition on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions.  By \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\),
\[
 M_i\mid A\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2),\qquad V_i=N^{-1}M_i-1/2.
\]
If \(N\) is even, the nearest nonzero lattice points are \(\pm N^{-1}\); if \(N\) is odd, they are \(\pm(2N)^{-1}\).  Each has positive binomial mass.  Thus \({\rm def:lattice-radius}\) implies
\[
 P\{0<|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\mid A\}>0,
\]
and \({\rm def:discrete-score}\) gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\).

The involution \(M_i\mapsto N-M_i\) preserves binomial mass and sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\).  The truncation indicator is even and the score is odd.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=1,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^3\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)^2}
 =\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}.
\]

Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Taylor's formula at \(1/2\) and \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) give
\[
 f_i(a,1/2+v)=f_i(a,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)v
 +\frac12\partial_x^2f_i(a,1/2)v^2+R_i(a,v),
 \qquad |R_i(a,v)|\leq \frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplication by \(q_{i,h}\), conditional expectation, and the three preceding moments yield
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A].
\]
On the support of the score, \(|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\), whence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A]\right|
 &\leq \frac{L}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[|V_i|^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]\\
 &\leq \frac{Lh_i(h)^2}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]
 =\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every division is justified by the strict positivity already proved.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the new derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy \( |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|\le L(8n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}N_i^{-1}+Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}\). Consequently, in the degree regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6, this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\), so their Gaussian theorem is an asymptotic benchmark for \(\theta_n\), not a finite-sample same-target result.
statements.justification: The bridge states exactly when the published finite indirect effect and the finite-population derivative are asymptotically interchangeable.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition 1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets.
statements.consumer: It permits valid asymptotic comparison with Theorem 6 while keeping the proposed finite-population derivative as a distinct target.
statements.proof_tex:
Work throughout conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\).  Define the proof-intermediate function
\[
g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}{2},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), if \(N_i=m>0\), then \(M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2)\), \(Z_i\) is independent of \(M_i\), and
\[
V_i=\frac{M_i-m/2}{m}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:anonymous-interference}\), \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\), and the preceding independence, the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) is
\[
\beta_i
:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right]
=4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right].
\]
For \(m=0\), the same definition gives \(\beta_i=0\), because then \(M_i-N_i/2=0\).  Thus
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For \(m>0\), write \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^m X_j\), where the \(X_j\) are independent and take the values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\) with equal probability.  Then \(V_i\) has the same conditional law as \(S_m/m\).  Independence and centering give
\[
\mathbb E S_m^2=\frac m4,\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^3=0,\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^4
=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
+6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\,\mathbb E X_k^2
=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E V_i=0,\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^3=0,\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le \frac{3}{16m^2}.
\]
The averaging defining \(g_i\), together with \(\texttt{ass:third-derivative-bound}\), yields
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|g_i^{(3)}(x)|\le L.
\]
Taylor's formula on \([0,1]\), applicable because \(1/2+V_i\in[0,1]\), therefore gives
\[
g_i(1/2+v)
=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
\qquad |R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying by \(v\), taking the conditional expectation, and using the four displayed moments gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
&=4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],\\
|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
&\le \frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\frac{3}{16m^2}
=\frac{L}{8m}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the coefficient of \(g_i'(1/2)\) is exactly \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\), while the constant and quadratic Taylor terms vanish because \(\mathbb E V_i=\mathbb E V_i^3=0\).

By \(\texttt{def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\).  If \(N_i=0\), \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\) gives
\[
|g_i'(1/2)|
\le \frac{|\partial_x f_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_x f_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
\le B.
\]
The triangle inequality, separated over nonisolated and isolated vertices, now proves the finite-sample claim:
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|
&\le \frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
+\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
&\le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
+\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to verify the stated scale comparison.  The conditions referred to as the Li--Wager Theorem~6 regime are recorded in \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\).  In particular, there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, eventually,
\[
\rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Indeed, this follows directly from \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\).  In the same regime, conditional on \(U_i=u\), the degree is binomial with \(n-1\) trials and success probability
\[
p_n(u)=\int_0^1\min\{1,\rho_nW(u,v)\}\,dv.
\]
Because \(0<\rho_n\le1\) and \(W\ge0\),
\[
\min\{1,\rho_nW(u,v)\}\ge \rho_n\min\{1,W(u,v)\}.
\]
The uniformly positive row-integral condition in that regime therefore supplies a constant \(c_{\rm deg}>0\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
\mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]=(n-1)p_n(u)\ge c_{\rm deg}(n-1)\rho_n.
\]
For completeness, the needed lower-tail bound follows directly from exponential Markov.  If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log 2\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(S\le\mu/2)
&\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb E e^{-tS}
=e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
&\le \exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
\le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) and \((1-\log 2)/2\ge1/8\) justify the last two inequalities.  Applying this bound conditionally on each \(U_i\) and then using the union bound yields, for
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\ge \frac{c_{\rm deg}}2(n-1)\rho_n\right\},
\]
the probability bound
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{c_{\rm deg}}8(n-1)\rho_n\right\}
\longrightarrow0,
\]
because \(n\rho_n\ge n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\) there are no isolates, and the finite-sample inequality already proved implies
\[
\frac{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
\le \frac{L}{4c_{\rm deg}(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}}
\longrightarrow0,
\]
since
\[
(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}\ge (1-o(1))n^{1/4+3\varepsilon/2}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The radii \(B\) and \(L\) are fixed model-class constants, as declared in the frozen core.  Hence, for every \(\eta>0\), the event in the preceding display is eventually contained in \(\{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|/\sqrt{\rho_n}\le\eta\}\), while \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_n^c)\to0\).  This is precisely
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]
The cited theorem is centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) on the \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale.  The last display makes its centering asymptotically compatible with \(\theta_n\) at that scale, while \(\texttt{def:target}\) and \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\) remain distinct finite-sample causal functionals.  This proves the final interpretation in the proposition.

statements.statement:
Fix \(0\leq m\leq\lfloor d/2\rfloor\) and write
\[
 K_m(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i\leq m\}.
\]
For every admissible \((U,A,Z)\)-marginal that remains in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) after adjoining independent Rademacher response signs, there is an explicit odd \(C^3\) degree-lattice bump whose derivative at one half has magnitude at least \(c a_m\), vanishes at every exposure lattice point of every degree at most \(m\), and yields
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|
 \geq \frac{c a_m}{n}\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac1n\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{n^{-1}\mathbb E_PK_m(A)}{n}}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{m,n}}{n}}.
\]
Thus the frozen mean-mass quantity \(a_m\sqrt{\pi_{m,n}/n}\) is an upper bound on the scale certified by this missing-sign experiment, not a lower bound without an additional count-concentration argument.  For \(m=0\), the certified isolate scale is \(B n^{-1}\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_0(A)}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact same-class finite-count obstruction furnished by a lattice-hidden random-response construction.
statements.gap: A first moment of the random low-degree count does not determine its square-root moment, and unconditional honest length can also spend its miscoverage budget on rare graph events.
statements.consumer: It prevents the mean-mass expression from being mislabeled as a proved minimax tail modulus and identifies the additional count-distribution information a matching result would require.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(m\geq1\), define the explicit odd function
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf1\{|t|\leq1/2\}.
\]
The fourth-order zero at each endpoint makes \(\phi\) a globally \(C^3\) function, and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  Let \(C_s=\|\phi^{(s)}\|_\infty\) for \(0\leq s\leq3\), choose a universal \(c_0>0\) with \(c_0\max_s C_s\leq1\), and set
\[
 g_m(x)=c_0a_m m^{-1}\phi\{m(x-1/2)\}.
\]
Because \(a_m\leq Bm^{-1}\) and \(a_m\leq Lm^{-2}\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \|g_m\|_\infty\leq B,\quad
 \|g_m'\|_\infty\leq B,\quad
 \|g_m''\|_\infty\leq B,\quad
 \|g_m'''\|_\infty\leq L,
\]
after decreasing \(c_0\) if necessary.  Also \(g_m'(1/2)=c_0a_m\).  Every noncentral exposure point of a degree \(N\leq m\) is at distance at least \((2N)^{-1}\geq(2m)^{-1}\) from one half; the central point is a zero of this odd bump.  Thus \(g_m\) vanishes at every such lattice point.  For \(m=0\), take \(g_0(x)=Bx\), which obeys all envelopes and vanishes at the only exposure of an isolate.

Adjoin independent Rademacher variables \(\varepsilon_i\), independent of \((U,A,Z)\), and let
\[
 f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_i g_m(x),\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The construction is i.i.d. across units and, by the preceding derivative bounds, satisfies \({\rm ass:unit-sampling}\), \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\), \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\), and \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\); retaining the admissible graph marginal preserves every other member property of \({\rm def:model-class}\).  Its target is
\[
 \theta_n=\frac{\beta_m}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\varepsilon_i,
 \qquad \beta_m=g_m'(1/2),
\]
with \(|\beta_m|=c_0a_m\) for \(m\geq1\) and \(|\beta_0|=B\).

If \(N_i\leq m\), then \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=0\) for every assignment, so the data contain no information about \(\varepsilon_i\).  No other unit's outcome contains \(f_i\), hence it contains no information about that sign either.  Enlarge the experiment by revealing every sign with \(N_i>m\).  Conditional on the enlarged data and \(A\), the remaining \(K_m(A)\) signs are still independent Rademacher variables.  Additional information can only decrease optimal risk, and zero is a median of their symmetric sum.  Consequently every estimator has conditional absolute risk at least
\[
 \frac{|\beta_m|}{n}\mathbb E\left[\left|\sum_{j=1}^{K_m(A)}\varepsilon_j\right|\Bigm|A\right].
\]
For \(S_k=\sum_{j=1}^k\varepsilon_j\), independence gives \(\mathbb ES_k^2=k\) and \(\mathbb ES_k^4=3k^2-2k\leq3k^2\).  If \(p_k=P\{S_k^2\geq k/2\}\), then decomposition at this event and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 k=\mathbb ES_k^2
 \leq\frac{k}{2}+(\mathbb ES_k^4)^{1/2}p_k^{1/2}
 \leq\frac{k}{2}+\sqrt3\,k p_k^{1/2}.
\]
Thus \(p_k\geq1/12\), and consequently
\[
 P\{|S_k|\geq\sqrt{k/2}\}\geq\frac1{12},
\]
so \(\mathbb E|S_k|\geq(12\sqrt2)^{-1}\sqrt k\).  Averaging over \(A\) proves the risk lower bound.

Finally, Jensen's inequality and the definition of \(\pi_{m,n}\) give
\[
 \frac1n\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}
 \leq\frac1n\sqrt{\mathbb E_PK_m(A)}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{m,n}}n}.
\]
The inequality is one-sided.  For example, if \(K\) is Bernoulli with mean \(p\) and \(np\to0\), then \(n^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt K=p/n\), whereas \(\sqrt{(p/n)/n}=\sqrt p/n\); their ratio tends to zero.  Thus a first-moment definition cannot supply the reverse inequality required by the frozen claim.

statements.statement: Let \(h=h^\dagger\). The feasible estimator and interval produced by \({\rm oeq:uniform-feasible-pc}\) satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|\lesssim\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\ge1-\alpha\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]\lesssim\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\). The pointwise certificate is exactly \(\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)/\sqrt\alpha\), including every realized degree and isolate.
statements.justification: This is a feasible finite-sample honest upper bound whose radius never silently discards low-degree units.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is asymptotic and targets its finite indirect effect; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest has neither graph dependence nor estimated spectral balancing.
statements.consumer: Experimenters can report the realized degree certificate before deciding whether to fund an ego-cluster follow-up.

statements.statement:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  These two displayed inequalities are only sufficient compatibility conditions for this witness; no characterization of nonemptiness and no converse outside this witness region is asserted.
statements.justification: The explicit equal-block graphon and three same-class response pairs prove the supported analytic converse whenever the displayed sufficient compatibility inequalities hold.
statements.gap: Whether the same converse holds for every nonempty compatible tuple outside the explicit block-witness region remains unresolved.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may treat the supported bandwidth envelope as a certified lower benchmark only when the graphon constants satisfy the displayed block compatibility conditions; otherwise the global converse is still open.
statements.proof_tex:
\textit{Step 1: the compatible block submodel.}
Let \(U_i\) be i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]\), use the cells, functions, and kernel displayed in the statement, and write \(T_0\) for the integral operator with kernel \(W_0\).  The intervals form a partition up to null endpoints.  Hence, for all \(1\leq k,\ell\leq r\),
\[
 \int_0^1\psi_k(u)\psi_\ell(u)\,du
 =r\,|I_k\cap I_\ell|=\mathbf 1\{k=\ell\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 (T_0\psi_k)(u)
 =c_0\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\int_{I_k}\sqrt r\,dv
 =\frac{c_0}{r}\psi_k(u).
\tag{2}
\]
The ranges of the \(r\) functions in (1) span the range of \(T_0\), so (2) proves that \(W_0\) has exact rank \(r\) and that every nonzero eigenvalue equals \(c_0/r\).  By the definition of \(c_0\),
\[
 \frac{c_0}{r}\geq\underline\lambda,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1W_0(u,v)\,dv=\frac{c_0}{r}\geq\kappa^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
The local condition \(c_0\leq\kappa\) gives \(0\leq W_0\leq\kappa\).  Together with \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\), it also gives
\[
 0\leq\rho_nW_0(u,v)\leq\rho_n\kappa\leq1,
\tag{4}
\]
so all Bernoulli edge probabilities are valid.

For completeness, we write out the Bernstein condition used in \({\rm ass:eigenfunction\text{-}bernstein}\): for a centered variable \(X\), it is
\[
 \mathbb E|X|^q\leq\frac{q!}{2}\mathbb E[X^2]b_\psi^{q-2},
 \qquad q\geq2.
\tag{5}
\]
Here \(\mathbb E\psi_k(U_i)=r^{-1/2}\).  If \(r\geq2\), then
\[
 \left|\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right|
 \leq\frac{r-1}{\sqrt r}\leq b_\psi.
\tag{6}
\]
Consequently, raising the bound in (6) to the power \(q-2\), multiplying by the square, and taking expectations gives
\[
 \mathbb E\left|\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right|^q
 \leq b_\psi^{q-2}\mathbb E\left[\left\{\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right\}^2\right]
 \leq\frac{q!}{2}b_\psi^{q-2}\mathbb E\left[\left\{\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{7}
\]
For \(r=1\) the centered variable is zero, so (5) is immediate.  Equations (1)--(7) verify orthonormality, exact rank, spectral strength, kernel bounds, row-mass regularity, the Bernstein moment condition, and edge-probability feasibility.  The i.i.d. latent types, the graph drawn conditionally according to \(W_0\), and the independent Bernoulli assignment then satisfy \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\), \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\), and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\).

Set \(s_0=B/4\) and let the i.i.d. intercepts \(\xi_i\), independent of all graph and assignment variables, have density
\[
p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}p_{s_0}(t)\,dt
 =s_0^{-1}\int_{-s_0}^{s_0}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)dt=1.
\]
For any deterministic \(g\in C^3[0,1]\), define the two response laws by
\[
 f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x),
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in[0,1].
\tag{9}
\]
Every construction below chooses \(g\) so that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq3B/4,
 \quad \|g'\|_\infty\leq B,
 \quad \|g''\|_\infty\leq B,
 \quad \|g'''\|_\infty\leq L.
\tag{10}
\]
Since \(|\xi_i|\leq B/4\), (10) verifies \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\); (9) verifies anonymous interference when inserted in \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\).  Thus, after (10) is checked separately for each \(g\), the induced laws are members of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), rather than merely oracle experiments outside the model.

Under (9), the target in \({\rm def:target}\) is nonrandom and equals
\[
 \theta_n^\pm=\pm g'(1/2),
 \qquad
 \Delta_g:=|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=2|g'(1/2)|.
\tag{11}
\]

\textit{Step 2: a common experiment-distance inequality.}
Let \(q_{s_0}=\sqrt{p_{s_0}}\).  The function \(q_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1/2}\cos(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\) is absolutely continuous after extension by zero, because it vanishes at both endpoints.  Its weak derivative satisfies
\[
 \|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2
 =\frac1{s_0}\left(\frac{\pi}{2s_0}\right)^2
 \int_{-s_0}^{s_0}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)dt
 =\frac{\pi^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{12}
\]
The fundamental theorem of calculus followed by Minkowski's integral inequality therefore yields, for every \(\eta_1,\eta_2\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 H^2\{p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1),p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\}
 =\|q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1)-q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\|_2^2
 \leq(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2\|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2
 =\frac{\pi^2(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{13}
\]
We use the convention in (13) for squared Hellinger distance.  Conditional on \((A,Z)\), the responses are independent translated intercepts.  If \(Q_g^+\) and \(Q_g^-\) denote the two observed-data laws, the product-affinity identity and \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\leq\sum_i x_i\) give, from (13) with translations differing by \(2g(X_i)\),
\[
 H^2(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng(X_i)^2,
 \qquad
 X_i=\begin{cases}1/2+V_i,&N_i>0,\\0,&N_i=0.\end{cases}
\tag{14}
\]
The outer expectation in (14) is valid because the law of \((A,Z)\) is identical in the two experiments.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq H(Q_g^+,Q_g^-).
\tag{15}
\]

\textit{Step 3: the linear graph-floor pair.}
Put \(\bar c=c_0/r\).  Conditional on \(U_i\), each other unit belongs to the same block with probability \(1/r\), independently, and the edge is then present with probability \(\rho_nc_0\).  Thus
\[
 N_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n),
 \qquad p_n=\frac{c_0d}{rn}=\frac{\bar c d}{n},
 \qquad \mu_n:=(n-1)p_n\asymp d.
\tag{16}
\]
Conditional on \(N_i=N>0\), Bernoulli randomization gives \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), whence
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mid A,N_i=N]=\frac1{4N}.
\tag{17}
\]
For a binomial variable with \(n-1\) trials,
\[
 \mathbb E\frac1{N_i+1}
 =\frac{1-(1-p_n)^n}{np_n}\leq\frac1{np_n}.
\tag{18}
\]
Since \(N^{-1}\leq2(N+1)^{-1}\) for \(N\geq1\), (17)--(18) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^nV_i^2\mathbf 1\{N_i>0\}
 =\frac n4\mathbb E\{N_i^{-1}\mathbf 1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq\frac{n}{2np_n}=O(n/d).
\tag{19}
\]
Also,
\[
 n\Pr(N_i=0)=n(1-p_n)^{n-1}
 \leq n e^{-\mu_n}=O(ne^{-c d})
\tag{20}
\]
for a constant \(c>0\) depending only on the fixed block parameters.

Take
\[
 g_G(x)=c_GB\sqrt{d/n}\,(x-1/2).
\tag{21}
\]
Because \(d/n\to0\), choosing \(c_G\leq1\) verifies all four inequalities in (10) for large \(n\).  By (19)--(21),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\sum_i g_G(X_i)^2
 &=c_G^2B^2\frac dn
 \left\{\mathbb E\sum_iV_i^2\mathbf 1(N_i>0)
       +\frac n4\Pr(N_i=0)\right\}\\
 &\leq Cc_G^2B^2\{1+d e^{-cd}\}\leq C'c_G^2B^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
Since \(s_0=B/4\), (14)--(15) and (22) show that \(c_G>0\) may be chosen, independently of \(n,d\), so that
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \eta:=(1-2\alpha)/2>0.
\tag{23}
\]
By (11) and (21), this pair has separation
\[
 \Delta_G=2c_GB\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{24}
\]

\textit{Step 4: the interior nonlinear bump.}
Fix the explicit odd function
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf 1\{|t|<1/2\}.
\tag{25}
\]
Its derivatives through order three match zero at \(\{-1/2,1/2\}\), so \(\phi\in C^3(\mathbb R)\), its support lies strictly inside \((-1,1)\), and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  For \(0\leq j_0\leq3\), let \(C_{j_0}=\|\phi^{(j_0)}\|_\infty<\infty\).  For \(d^{-1}\leq h\leq d^{-1/2}\), set
\[
 g_h(x)=c_ILh^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{h}\right).
\tag{26}
\]
Then
\[
 \|g_h^{(j_0)}\|_\infty=c_ILh^{3-j_0}C_{j_0},
 \qquad 0\leq j_0\leq3.
\tag{27}
\]
Choose \(c_I C_3\leq1\).  Since \(d\geq C_{\log}\log n\) implies \(h\leq d^{-1/2}\to0\), (27) verifies (10) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(B,L\).

We next prove the local binomial-mass bound used in (14).  For \(N\geq1\), the largest atom of \({\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\) is at most \(C/\sqrt N\).  Indeed, for \(N=2q_0\), if \(a_{q_0}={2q_0\choose q_0}4^{-q_0}\), then \(a_0=1\),
\[
 \frac{a_{q_0+1}}{a_{q_0}}=\frac{2q_0+1}{2q_0+2},
 \qquad
 \left(\frac{2q_0+1}{2q_0+2}\right)^2\leq\frac{q_0+1}{q_0+2},
\tag{28}
\]
so induction gives \(a_{q_0}\leq(q_0+1)^{-1/2}\); the odd case is bounded by the preceding even case.  The interval \(|M/N-1/2|\leq h\) contains at most \(2Nh+2\) integers.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr\{|M/N-1/2|\leq h\mid N\}
 \leq C(\sqrt N h+N^{-1/2}).
\tag{29}
\]
For \(N_i\) in (16), exponential Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{-tN_i}\) with \(t=\log2\) gives \(\Pr(N_i<\mu_n/2)\leq e^{-\mu_n/8}\).  Jensen's inequality and a split at \(\mu_n/2\) then give
\[
 \mathbb E\sqrt{N_i}\leq\sqrt{\mu_n},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1/2}\mathbf 1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq\sqrt{2/\mu_n}+e^{-\mu_n/8}.
\tag{30}
\]
Combining (29)--(30), using \(\mu_n\asymp d\) and \(h\geq d^{-1}\), yields the uniform bound
\[
 \Pr(|V_i|\leq h,N_i>0)\leq C\sqrt d\,h.
\tag{31}
\]
The bump is zero for isolates and outside the event in (31).  Hence (14), (26), and (31) imply
\[
 H^2(Q_h^+,Q_h^-)
 \leq Cc_I^2n\sqrt d\,L^2h^7.
\tag{32}
\]
For \(L>0\), define the proof-intermediate bandwidth
\[
 h_0=\left(\frac{L^{-2}}{n\sqrt d}\right)^{1/7}.
\tag{33}
\]
When \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), substituting \(h=h_0\) in (32) leaves the right-hand side bounded by \(Cc_I^2\).  Decreasing \(c_I\), if necessary, makes the total variation at most \(\eta\).  Equations (11), (26), and (33) give
\[
 \Delta_I=2c_ILh_0^2
 =2c_IL^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{34}
\]

\textit{Step 5: the invisible degree-lattice bump.}
Let \(D_n=\lceil Kd\rceil\), where \(K>e\bar c\) is fixed sufficiently large.  For \(t>0\), exponential Markov's inequality and \(1+y\leq e^y\) give
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n)
 \leq e^{-tD_n}(1-p_n+p_ne^t)^{n-1}
 \leq\exp\{-tD_n+\mu_n(e^t-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log(D_n/\mu_n)\) when \(D_n\geq\mu_n\) yields
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n)\leq\left(\frac{e\mu_n}{D_n}\right)^{D_n}
 \leq e^{-a_Kd}.
\tag{35}
\]
Choose \(K\) so large that \(a_KC_{\log}>2\).  The union bound and \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\) give
\[
 \Pr\left(\max_iN_i>D_n\right)
 \leq ne^{-a_Kd}=o(1).
\tag{36}
\]
Put \(w_n=(4D_n)^{-1}\) and
\[
 g_D(x)=c_D Lw_n^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{w_n}\right),
\tag{37}
\]
where \(c_DC_3\leq1\).  The analogue of (27), together with \(D_n\to\infty\), verifies (10) for large \(n\).  If \(1\leq N_i\leq D_n\), every noncentral point of the exposure lattice has
\[
 |V_i|\geq\begin{cases}N_i^{-1},&N_i\text{ even},\\(2N_i)^{-1},&N_i\text{ odd},\end{cases}
 \geq(2D_n)^{-1}>w_n.
\tag{38}
\]
At the central point \(V_i=0\), oddness gives \(g_D(1/2)=0\); for an isolate, \(g_D(0)=0\).  Thus on \(E_n=\{\max_iN_i\leq D_n\}\), every observed response equals \(\xi_i\) under both signs.  The restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_n\) are identical, and (36) consequently implies
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_D^+,Q_D^-)
 \leq\Pr(E_n^c)=o(1).
\tag{39}
\]
On the other hand, (11) and (37) give
\[
 \Delta_D=2c_D Lw_n^2\asymp Ld^{-2}.
\tag{40}
\]
This proves invisibility from the actual lattice, rather than putting that property into the construction by definition.

\textit{Step 6: risk and honest-length reductions.}
Consider any one of the three pairs above and abbreviate its targets by \(\theta^+,\theta^-\), its observed laws by \(Q^+,Q^-\), and its separation by \(\Delta\).  For an arbitrary estimator \(T\), let \(A_T=\{|T-\theta^+|\geq\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_T^c\), the triangle inequality gives \(|T-\theta^-|\geq\Delta/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}|T-\theta^+|+\mathbb E_{Q^-}|T-\theta^-|
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{Q^+(A_T)+Q^-(A_T^c)\}\\
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{41}
\]
Thus the larger of the two risks is at least \(\Delta\{1-\operatorname{TV}\}/4\).

Now let \(\mathcal C\) be any confidence interval having coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under every member of the class.  Total variation and the union bound imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q^+\{\theta^+,\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}
 &\geq Q^+\{\theta^+\in\mathcal C\}
       +Q^+\{\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}-1\\
 &\geq(1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-))-1\\
 &=1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{42}
\]
An interval containing both target values has length at least \(\Delta\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)
 \geq\Delta\{1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
\tag{43}
\]
By (23), (32)--(34), and (39), all pairwise total variations are eventually at most \(\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2\).  Equations (41) and (43), followed by the infima in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), therefore yield the lower orders in (24), (34), and (40) for both \(R^*_{n,d,L}\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\).

\textit{Step 7: comparison with the bandwidth envelope.}
Write \(a_n=(n\sqrt d)^{-1/2}\).  For \(L>0\), (33) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2=a_nh_0^{-3/2}=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{44}
\]
If \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), evaluate the infimum in \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\) at \(h=d^{-1}\).  The condition \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\) is equivalent to \(L^2\geq d^{13/2}/n\), and hence
\[
 a_nd^{3/2}=d^{5/4}n^{-1/2}\leq Ld^{-2},
 \qquad
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{45}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), evaluation at \(h_0\), using (44), gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{46}
\]
If \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\), then \(L^2\leq d^3/n\).  Evaluation at \(h=d^{-1/2}\) gives
\[
 Ld^{-1}\leq\sqrt{d/n},
 \qquad
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{47}
\]
For \(L=0\), the infimum is attained at \(d^{-1/2}\) and equals \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  In the first regime, combine the graph pair (24) and lattice pair (40); in the second, combine (24) and (34); and in the third and in the case \(L=0\), use (24).  Since \(\max\{x,y\}\geq(x+y)/2\), (45)--(47) show that both minimax criteria are bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of
\[
 \sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \left\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\right\}
 =\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\tag{48}
\]
All constants used to make the experiment distances small depend only on the fixed class constants and \(\alpha\), not on \(n,d\).  This completes the conditional block-submodel converse and does not extend it beyond the two sufficient compatibility inequalities in the statement.

statements.statement:
For \(L>0\), the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  The explicit degree-exact procedure proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the unchanged class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  The three analytic phases are therefore not asserted to be minimax matched: the supported lower experiments remain open, and the tail first moment \(\pi_{m,n}\) does not by itself determine the exact missing-sign scale.
statements.justification: This gives the exact analytic bandwidth phases and the finite-sample upper inequalities without labeling them minimax matched.
statements.gap: The supported-unit converse and an unconditional tail-adaptive procedure remain open.
statements.consumer: A platform can distinguish bandwidth geometry from the still-unproved optimality and isolate-adaptation questions.

statements.statement: On the predeclared sharp-radius class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), evaluate \({\rm def:radii}\) and \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) at \(L=0\). Then \(h_0=\infty\), \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), and the positive-degree Taylor term in \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)\) is identically zero. The exact moment equation \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\) also cancels every quadratic exposure response, with affine responses as a special case. At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the nonremainder supported-unit score and graph contributions have order \(\sqrt{d/n}\), while the complete degree-exact certificate retains \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)=Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}\) and \(\overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2=C_{\mathrm{pc}}B^2n^{-2}\{\sum_{i:N_i>0}\mu_{2,i}(h_\star)^{-1}+\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\}+\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}\). An affine realized law inside \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) with \(L>0\) does not permit setting the honesty radius to zero; the reduction applies only when \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) is fixed before observing the experiment.
statements.justification: This sanity reduction shows that the exact score has no positive-degree approximation bias on the class whose third-derivative radius is fixed at zero, without hiding isolates or feasible-PC error.
statements.gap: Existing graphon-interference asymptotics do not state this degree-exact zero-remainder reduction or distinguish a predeclared zero-radius class from an affine realization inside a positive-radius honesty class.
statements.consumer: Analysts who prespecify the sharp class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) can use the largest bandwidth and report the supported-unit graph-floor certificate together with the visible isolate and feasible-PC remainders.

statements.statement:
Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the unchanged class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Hence the isolate term in the conditional certificate cannot be replaced by \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\).  The latter is an unconditional missing-sign fluctuation scale, not a conditional identification radius.  This does not rule out a different, unconditionally honest procedure that abandons the graph-only conditional-bias guarantee; no such procedure is constructed here.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a realized graph \(A\) and let \(S_0=\{i:N_i=0\}\).  Consider the single admissible response law
\[
 f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx,
 \qquad \varepsilon_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim{\rm Unif}\{-1,1\},
\]
independent of the graph variables.  It obeys the response envelope because \(|f_i(a,x)|\leq B\), \(|\partial_xf_i(a,x)|=B\), and its second and third derivatives vanish; thus it also obeys the third-derivative bound for every \(L\geq0\).  Its use does not alter any graph, rank, support, or randomization property of \({\rm def:model-class}\).

Condition on two response-sign configurations that agree on \(S_0^c\) and are opposite on \(S_0\).  Both configurations have positive conditional probability under this one i.i.d. response law.  For every isolate, anonymous interference gives
\[
 Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=f_i(Z_i,0)=0,
\]
and an isolate's response sign enters no other unit's response.  Hence the complete conditional observed-data laws are identical under the two configurations.  Their targets, however, differ by
\[
 \frac{2B}{n}|S_0|=\frac{2B}{n}I_0(A).
\]
If \(m(A)\) denotes the common conditional mean of an arbitrary estimator under these indistinguishable configurations and \(\theta^+,\theta^-\) their targets, the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \max\{|m(A)-\theta^+|,|m(A)-\theta^-|\}
 \geq\frac12|\theta^+-\theta^-|
 =\frac{B}{n}I_0(A).
\]
Therefore any common graph-only conditional-bias radius valid for every response configuration must be at least this large.  The argument is pointwise in \(A\), so averaging cannot turn this conditional radius into the smaller centered fluctuation scale.
statements.justification: The two response-sign configurations are conditionally observationally equivalent on every realized isolate, which forces the full isolate allowance for any graph-only conditional-bias certificate.
statements.gap: This is a conditional impossibility result; it deliberately does not claim that every unconditionally honest procedure must pay the same expected length.
statements.consumer: Analysts must retain the realized isolate contribution when using the conditional smoothness certificate, or explicitly change the inferential target or conditioning convention.

Conditionally on \(A\), write \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\), \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)^\top\), and \(q_h=(q_{1,h},\ldots,q_{n,h})^\top\).  For a centered scalar function \(g(X)\), define its first projection as \(g^{(1)}=\sum_j\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]\) and its second projection as
\[
 g^{(2)}=\sum_{j<k}\left\{\mathbb E[g\mid X_j,X_k]
 -\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]-\mathbb E[g\mid X_k]\right\},
\]
and apply these definitions coordinatewise to a vector.  The first two conditional Hoeffding projections of the exact-support score satisfy
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0
\]
simultaneously for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Consequently, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\) and condition on \(A\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), the \(N_i\) neighbor contrasts are exchangeable.  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\) and \(V_i=N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}X_k\),
\[
 1=\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_k\mid A]
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_j\mid A].
\]
If \(A_{ij}=0\), then \(q_{i,h}\) is independent of the centered variable \(X_j\), so the same expectation is zero.  Since \(\mathbb E_ZX_j^2=1/4\), the orthogonal projection of \(q_{i,h}\) onto the span of \(X_j\) is \(4A_{ij}X_j\).  Summing over \(j\) proves \(q_h^{(1)}=4AX\), uniformly in \(h\).

For the second projection, the simultaneous sign reversal of all neighbor contrasts sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\), hence sends the odd score \(q_{i,h}\) to \(-q_{i,h}\).  For distinct \(j,k\), integrate over all contrasts except \((X_j,X_k)\).  The resulting function on \(\{-1/2,1/2\}^2\) is odd under \((X_j,X_k)\mapsto(-X_j,-X_k)\).  Its Walsh expansion therefore contains only the two degree-one monomials and no constant or degree-two monomial.  After subtraction of the first projections, the \(\{j,k\}\) interaction is zero.  This proves \(q_h^{(2)}=0\).

An \(A\)-measurable linear map preserves Hoeffding order, proving the two displayed identities with \(I_n-\Pi\).  Finally, conditional independence and \(\mathbb E_Z[XX^\top\mid A]=I_n/4\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2
 =16\operatorname{tr}\!\left((I_n-\Pi)AA^\top(I_n-\Pi)\frac{I_n}{4}\right)
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2,
\]
where symmetry of \(A\) and idempotence of \(I_n-\Pi\) justify the last equality.
statements.justification: This is the exact early-kill calculation required to decide whether spectral balancing itself introduces a bandwidth-dependent first- or second-order term.
statements.gap: The identity is exact on the binomial lattice and is not supplied by global-score graphon projector results.
statements.consumer: It is the load-bearing decomposition used by the explicit PC conditional certificate.

statements.statement:
For the explicit construction in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), all distinct scores over \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) can be represented and computed in polynomial time.  Conditional on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\}\geq1-\alpha\).  If \(C_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)A\) and
\[
 G_A(C_A)=\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2,
\]
then the explicit bias certificate also satisfies the deterministic bound
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq \frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*
      +B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}{n}}.
\]
The exact first two Hoeffding projections create no bandwidth-dependent term.  This result does not assert the sharper uniform rates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\); the displayed graph norm and conservative variance certificate are the proved computable quantities under the frozen assumptions.
statements.justification: This gives an explicit polynomial-time first-projection PC estimator and a finite-sample conditional certificate without asserting the unproved sharp spectral remainder rates.
statements.gap: The exact first two Hoeffding projections are benign, but the frozen assumptions do not yet yield the edge-restricted projector norm and sharp product-ANOVA bounds needed for a \(d/n\) variance remainder.
statements.consumer: The observable certificate is safe for experiment reporting; its conservative variance term transparently signals that the sharp confidence-length frontier remains unresolved.

For every parameter tuple satisfying the displayed model conditions for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, but which need not satisfy \(\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\}\leq\kappa\) and \(b_\psi\geq(r-1)/\sqrt r\), does there exist a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\)?  The handle is to characterize enough of the compatibility region for bounded nonnegative exact-rank graphons, then build within each compatible class analogues of the linear, smooth-bump, and exposure-lattice experiments from \({\rm thm:minimax\text{-}lower}\).  The block construction proves the result only on its explicit sufficient region; it does not characterize nonemptiness outside that region.
statements.justification: The proved block witness covers an explicit sufficient compatibility region but the model-class parameters do not encode the full nonemptiness region.
statements.gap: A compatible exact-rank bounded nonnegative graphon need not contain the equal-block witness, and no replacement family is yet known uniformly over every nonempty tuple.
statements.consumer: Its resolution determines whether the supported analytic envelope is a global minimax converse or only a certified conditional benchmark.

sampling_model.units: One triangular-array population with independent preassignment draws \((U_i,f_i)\); the finite-population derivative is realized after this draw.
sampling_model.network: One observed undirected graph drawn conditionally independently from the sparse finite-rank graphon \(\rho_nW\), with \(\rho_n=d/n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment is independent of the neighbor count conditional on the preassignment graph.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is known and fixed at one half; each positive realized degree uses its exact nearest nonzero exposure support, and isolates remain explicitly unsupported.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Graphon eigenfunctions are replaced by the leading empirical eigenspace; leave-one-edge-out residualization returns observable bias and variance remainder certificates.
sampling_model.inference_randomness: Coverage and risk average over the declared preassignment unit draw, graph draw, and Bernoulli assignment, as in the retained model; graph-observable radii expose the realized support contribution.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a Gaussian limit at \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale for the PC-balancing estimator centered at both the population indirect effect and the finite indirect effect under its polynomial-degree sparse regime.
Theorem 2.1 and Section 3 incorporate worst-case smoothness bias into honest fixed-length confidence intervals and bandwidth choice in nonparametric regression.
Theorems 1--3 use between-class and ordered moduli to bound expected length of honest adaptive confidence intervals.
The average direct and indirect effects decompose the derivative of Bernoulli policy value.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic benchmark. Proposition 1, equations (4)--(5), relates its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, and Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limit for its PC estimator in a polynomial-degree sparse regime. The present target \(\theta_n\) is a new realized finite-population derivative; \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives the exact degree-level comparison, so no finite-sample same-target tightening is claimed. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform the empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control an exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is cited only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks; the separate arXiv identifier 2504.06108 is omitted because its current contagion manuscript is not the linear-rate comparator described in the earlier core.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\). These identities do not establish the feasible spectral remainders. Isolates have no exposure variation, so the safe interval adds their full derivative envelope. Under i.i.d. preassignment responses, the corresponding same-class testing modulus is smaller, of order \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\); closing that upper--lower gap requires an estimator, not a stronger assumption.
honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is only an asymptotic benchmark after \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\). Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius; isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a proposed matching converse, and the same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus is explicit. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) upper allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. The open tail-adaptive construction must retain the i.i.d. \((U_i,f_i)\) class and the stated conditioning convention. Unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside scope.
